translationRepairs: A granddaughter of Yuwen Jiong was exceptionally beautiful and was already in the palace.
A granddaughter of Yuchi Jiong was exceptionally beautiful and was already in the palace.
s0127 has 尉遲迥女孫; 尉遲 is the Xianbei surname Yuchi, not Yuwen (宇文). The proposed Yuchi Jiong correctly identifies the grandfather named in the kinship phrase.
A granddaughter of Yuwen Jiong had beautiful looks and was already in the palace.
A granddaughter of Yuchi Jiong had beautiful looks and was already in the palace.
The literal likewise misreads 尉遲迥 as Yuwen Jiong; Yuchi Jiong is the correct romanization of the same Chinese name.
Gao Feng, Yang Su, and others overtook him, seized his horse's bridle, and remonstrated with him in desperate earnest.
Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and others overtook him, seized his horse's bridle, and remonstrated with him in desperate earnest.
s0131 names 高熲; 熲 is read Jiǒng, so Gao Jiong is required. Feng is a mistransliteration of that character.
Gao Feng said, "Your Majesty, would you slight the realm under Heaven for the sake of one woman!"
Gao Jiong said, "Your Majesty, would you slight the realm under Heaven for the sake of one woman!"
s0133 attributes the speech to 高熲; the speaker must be Gao Jiong, not Gao Feng.
At first, because Gao Feng had been a retainer in her father's household, the empress treated him with great intimacy and respect.
At first, because Gao Jiong had been a retainer in her father's household, the empress treated him with great intimacy and respect.
s0138 again names 高熲 as the father's household guest; Gao Jiong restores the correct personal name.
Through this she urged the emperor to dismiss Gao Feng, and in the end the crown prince was deposed and Prince Guang of Jin was made heir. All of this was the empress's doing.
Through this she urged the emperor to dismiss Gao Jiong, and in the end the crown prince was deposed and Prince Guang of Jin was made heir. All of this was the empress's doing.
s0143 has 黜高熲; the official dismissed is Gao Jiong. Feng remains a mistransliteration of 熲.
When he arrived, the empress wept and bowed in apology. Feng, Su, and the others brought about a reconciliation.
When he arrived, the empress wept and bowed in apology. Jiong, Su, and the others brought about a reconciliation.
s0136 shortens the name to 熲 beside 素; the given-name reference must be Jiong, matching Gao Jiong, not Feng.
Now, hearing that Feng had called her a mere woman, she bore a deep grudge against him.
Now, hearing that Jiong had called her a mere woman, she bore a deep grudge against him.
s0139 has 聞熲謂己為一婦人; the short reference 熲 is Jiong, not Feng.

When Feng's principal wife died and his concubine bore a son, she thought even less of him and gradually slandered him to the emperor. The emperor, for his part, followed her word in almost every matter.

When Jiong's principal wife died and his concubine bore a son, she thought even less of him and gradually slandered him to the emperor. The emperor, for his part, followed her word in almost every matter.
s0140 has 熲夫人; the possessive short form of 高熲 must be Jiong's, not Feng's.
He then called Minister of War Liu Xu and Palace Attendant Yuan Yan and said, "Summon my son!"
He then called Minister of War Liu Shu and Palace Attendant Yuan Yan and said, "Summon my son!"
s0164 names 兵部尚書柳述; 述 is Shù, so Liu Shu is correct and Xu misreads the given name.
Xiao Kui brought her from her uncle's house and had the envoy cast lots for her. The result was auspicious."
Xiao Kui brought her from her uncle's house and had the envoy cast lots for her. The result was auspicious.
The idiomatic ends with a stray closing quotation mark after “auspicious” with no matching opener for that clause; removing it restores clean punctuation without changing meaning.
